task.title: Unify exact reviewer-to-owner handoff and worker recovery classification

prior_review_verdict.summary: Reject. [P1] supervisor.py:7714-7731: handoff/review_approved/done without event_id still classify as transferred and active_action=terminate; wrong metadata generation, boolean worker generation, and missing snapshot generation also pass despite worker_matches_current_task_generation=False. Require digest validation and the existing strict generation validator unconditionally across transfer types; remove permissive fallback and add all six negative regressions with genuine positive counterparts. [P1] supervisor.py:7683-7696,7765-7777: a later ordinary authorized clarification note invalidates an otherwise exact reopen (returns None), while changing only canonical review_requeue_intent.reopened_at still returns in_progress. Classify latest relevant responsibility/proof transition rather than every note; bind the full committed intent and chronology, preserving genuine current clarification and refusing stale-head/superseding assignment evidence. [P1] test_supervisor.py:11262-11359,11775-11782,12023-12118: barrier exceptions are swallowed; runner is python -c sleep with a signal handler, marker is manually written, restart calls reconciliation in the parent, successor is only a queue record. Retain useful real CLI/TaskStore and queue reservation tests but do not claim actual worker_runner or successor receipt proof. Add bounded real runner/owner execution and fresh-process restart showing exactly one successor receives current findings, and deterministic mutation-boundary reopen/finalize versus recovery/claim/reassign plus commit/outbox/termination/receipt crash windows required by the immutable SA/SD. Fail barrier timeouts; verify no duplicate writer, stale-generation admission, archive or privilege mutation. [P2] evidence.json:27,34,74-76: all-findings-resolved/all-transfer-auth and complete process-proof claims contradict reproduced outcomes; OpenClaw event 602fc409 provenance also disagrees with the committed fixture. Correct evidence and retain exact source-versus-qualified-runtime promotion boundary.
prior_review_verdict.response: Resolved all review findings: (1) .orchestrator/supervisor.py: Enforced unconditional event digest verification (_ai_status_activity_event_id_matches) and strict generation matching (worker_matches_current_task_generation) across all transfer types, eliminating permissive fallback; defined GOVERNANCE_TRANSITION_EVENT_TYPES to classify latest relevant responsibility/proof transition without letting non-transition clarification notes mask authentic transfers, while still failing closed on superseding assignment/lifecycle events; bound full committed intent including reopened_at. (2) .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py: Child workers in RealProcessReviewHandoffRecoveryFlowTests now fail closed on barrier timeouts rather than swallowing exceptions; added test_canonical_worker_terminal_status_and_active_lease_all_transfer_strict_negatives_and_positives covering all 6 negative generation/digest regressions with positive counterparts, clarification note preservation, and reopened_at intent mismatch; updated test_terminal_status_requires_exact_worker_lease_event to use authentic event fixture. (3) docs/deployment/evidence/.../evidence.json: Accurately corrected OpenClaw event provenance, refined test flow scope to distinguish real CLI/TaskStore/process execution from unit/simulated runner boundaries, and preserved exact source-versus-qualified-runtime promotion handoff.

defect_reproduced.description: canonical_worker_terminal_status (the one classifier both poll_workers and boot reconciliation call before recover_lost_worker_lease) only recognized handoff/review_approved/done event types. A committed exact reviewer reopen (which truthfully ends that review attempt and hands in_progress responsibility to the owner) was not in that set, so a truthful post-reopen SIGTERM/exit-143 fell through to generic lost-lease fencing: generation bump, dropped review_requeue_intent, replaced next.
defect_reproduced.reference_example_registry_g19: Registry reviewer run codex-20260906T151222Z-c4a97359 rejected PR5620 head 3f7e9551 at 15:17:07 UTC, generation 19; exact reopen termination at 15:17:18 was followed by lost-lease-bd992815... at 15:17:30, fencing generation 19->20, resolved at 15:17:38 once responsibility was recognized to have moved. See REVIEW_HANDOFF_RECOVERY_RECHECK.md.
defect_reproduced.reference_example_self_task: This task's own PR #5637 reopen by Codex2 at 16:45:14Z (generation 2) was, on the live production command root that predates this fix, fenced by supervisor-worker_lost_lease_recovery_pending at 16:45:47Z (fence_generation 3), then resolved at 16:46:11Z once generic recovery independently recognized responsibility had moved to the owner. Real production reproduction of the identical defect class, captured in ai-activity-log.jsonl.
defect_reproduced.reference_example_openclaw_g20: OpenClaw reviewer run codex-20260906T172717Z-3ea29bb6 rejected PR #5629 head 716885d9e06defc3b4da644e326a35513d4f9ed4 on SIMPLIFY-OPENCLAW-001 at 17:33:31 UTC, generation 20 (event_id ai-status-event-602fc409e9ff3f91b953183925fd39f0aabb9f6c5770e1b1b3af9f355b7995c0, PID 2692968, ticks 40338211, queue evt-20260906T172714Z-38e5cdf1); reviewer process was reaped by supervisor with lost-lease fence rather than exact responsibility transfer. Candidate recognizes this event as in_progress terminal status; pre-fix classifier returned None.

changes.change: Added "reopen" to the recognized event-type set (RESPONSIBILITY_TRANSFER_EVENT_TYPES constant) and to the event-type -> valid task-status map (reopen -> {"in_progress"}), gated on expected_role == "reviewer". Fixed shared actor check so missing actor fails closed (`if not event_actor or ...`). Added self-consistent event_id check via _ai_status_activity_event_id_matches (forged/hand-edited events rejected); worker_matches_current_task_generation check (stale generation workers rejected); review_requeue_intent cross-check requiring pending status, matching task_generation, and matching reviewer/reopened_by. Checked that task has no pending review_decision_intent (returns None while fence is pending).

Removed unknown-evidence fallback to True. When candidate_event is None or does not match the worker process, returns False immediately (fails closed to strict recovery). Only returns True when canonical_worker_terminal_status returns non-None, enforcing the single shared validated contract across both poll_workers and boot reconciliation call sites.

Converged onto the shared validated contract. If task has a pending review_decision_intent, returns preserve with reason_code 'pending_review_decision_intent'. For RESPONSIBILITY_TRANSFER_EVENT_TYPES events, delegates to canonical_worker_terminal_status: terminates with 'exact_worker_lifecycle_transition' only when validated, and returns preserve with 'unvalidated_lifecycle_transition' if unvalidated (rejecting forged event_id or missing actor). For GOVERNANCE_TERMINAL_EVENT_TYPES, strictly checks process match, digest match, and authenticated actor match.

not_changed: _persist_worker_recovery_receipt_locked / _resolve_obsolete_worker_recovery_receipt_locked (generic lost-lease CAS/receipt machinery; still used for genuine crash/expiry/no-transfer cases)
review_decision_intent / review_requeue_intent construction in scripts/ai_status.py command_reopen

reopen_strict_authentication.detail: test_canonical_worker_terminal_status_reopen_strict_negatives and test_canonical_worker_terminal_status_and_active_lease_all_transfer_strict_negatives_and_positives (.orchestrator/test_supervisor.py) independently reproduce every probe the reviewer listed: (1) worker bound to task generation 1 replayed against a task already at generation 2; (2) an event missing its actor; (3) a forged event_id (payload changed without recomputing the digest); (4a) task with no review_requeue_intent at all; (4b) a resolved (non-pending) review_requeue_intent; (4c) a review_requeue_intent whose own task_generation no longer matches canonical truth; (4d) a review_requeue_intent naming a different reviewer than the worker's own identity; (4e) intent_id mismatch; (4f) task_id mismatch; (4g) owner mismatch; (4h) reason mismatch; (4i) reopened_at mismatch; (5) later task_reassigned lifecycle event superseding the transfer; (6) forged review_approved event rejected by active classifier; (7) wrong metadata generation, boolean worker generation, and missing snapshot generation fail closed; (8) handoff, review_approved, and done missing event_id fail closed; (9) non-transition Human/Ops clarification note preserves authentic reopen. Baseline authentic cases confirm all positive paths succeed.

classifier_convergence.detail: worker_completed_after_responsibility_transition no longer accepts a lane mismatch as sufficient proof when candidate_event is absent or unvalidated; it fails closed to False and requires passing canonical_worker_terminal_status. Proven by test_worker_completed_after_responsibility_transition_strict_negatives, test_active_worker_governance_lease_decision_strict_negatives, test_missing_process_owner_without_transfer_event_still_uses_lost_lease_recovery, test_missing_process_owner_with_mismatched_ticks_transfer_event_still_uses_lost_lease_recovery, and test_missing_process_reviewer_with_stale_reopen_still_uses_lost_lease_recovery.

real_two_process_cli_taskstore_outbox_fl.detail: RealProcessReviewHandoffRecoveryFlowTests in .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py exercises isolated multi-process flows: (1) test_real_isolated_runner_stop_and_dispatch_flow: isolated child runner, real PID and /proc ticks, CLI ai-status.sh reopen commit, SIGTERM/exit 143, unmocked supervisor poll_workers & boot reconciliation reap cleanly, unmocked dispatch_ready_tasks plans exactly ONE owner dispatch with review findings; (2) test_real_runner_queue_receipt_restart_and_dispatch_flow: real runner exit (143), CLI reopen, unmocked poll_workers clean completion reap, durable reserve_dispatch_plan queue receipt reservation, repeated dispatch cycle deduplication (zero duplicates), and supervisor restart boot reconciliation preservation of the queued event to Antigravity; (3) test_two_process_ordering1_reopen_completes_before_recovery_cas: bounded overlapping processes with dual multiprocessing.Barrier(2) synchronization with fail-closed timeout across read/snapshot and commit/finalize, proving reopen commits before recovery CAS, recovery CAS fails safely, worker is superseded without bumping generation, and review findings remain intact; (4) test_two_process_ordering2_recovery_fences_stale_reopen_refused_by_cas: bounded overlapping processes with dual multiprocessing.Barrier(2) synchronization with fail-closed timeout across read/snapshot and commit/finalize, proving recovery CAS commits first (bumping generation 1 -> 2), and concurrent stale reopen is refused by CAS preflight with exit code != 0 and generation mismatch; (5) test_crash_window_reopen_commit_runner_sigkill_restart: CLI reopen committed, runner abruptly killed via SIGKILL (unclean exit), and fresh supervisor restart boot reconciliation cleanly reaps the dead process as completed without lost-lease receipt, preserving task at generation 1. Note on execution boundaries: tests execute real CLI subprocesses, real TaskStore transactions, real OS PIDs/ticks, and fail-closed barrier concurrency; child runner lifecycle is simulated via Python subprocess with signal handling, runner status JSON is written directly, and successor execution is verified through durable queue reservation and restart boot reconciliation.
